To Mei Pao and other local newspapers:

BODY OF CHEN LOH TO BE ENCOFFINED TO-DAY

In connection with the murder of Li Kuo-
chieh (李國杰), the eldest grandson of the late Marquis
Li Hung-chang, which took place on February 21 at the
entrance of Sim Yuan Tsung (沁園邨) on Sinza Road,
many Japanese and puppet officials called at the Greater
Shanghai Funeral Directors yesterday to pay their last
respects to the deceased as he was one of the promoters
and organizers of the "Reformed Government".
The body of Chen Loh (陳籙), Minister
of Foreign Affairs, who was killed at his home on Tseng
Ching Road in Chinese controlled territory on the night of
the Chinese New Year Day, has also been removed to the
Greater Shanghai Funeral Directors.
Chen Loh's encoffining ceremony will be held to-day
when Japanese and puppet officials will be present to
offer their condolence to the family of the deceased.
As a precaution against untoward incidents,
the Police will detail a number of Foreign and Chinese
detectives for duty at the place.

鉴于前李鸿章侯爵之长孙李国杰（Li Kuo-chieh）于2月21日在新闸路沁园邨入口处被谋杀一事，许多日本人和伪政权官员昨日前往大上海殡仪馆向死者致以最后的敬意，因为他是“维新政府”的发起人和组织者之一。
在农历新年当晚于华界曾精路家中遇害的外交部长陈籙（Chen Loh）的遗体，也被移送至大上海殡仪馆。
陈籙的入殓仪式将于今日举行，届时日本人和伪政权官员将出席，向死者家属表示慰问。
为防范意外事件，警方将派遣多名外籍和华籍侦探在现场执勤。

CHINA PRESS
FEB 21 1939
（印：SA ... N ... 68180 ...）

Death Bullets Strike
Down Puppet Minister
In Shanghai Residence

Raiders From Badlands
Grim Guests At New
Year Festival

NIPPON GENDARMES
INVESTIGATE CASE

Chen Lo's Guards Hold
Hands As Gunmen Throw
Guests Into Confusion

Chen Lo, puppet "foreign minister" of the Nanking regime, was host to death in his residence at House 25, Lane 668, Yu Yuen Road, on Sunday night, when six armed men burst their way into his sitting room and shot the official as he lolled on a couch.

Seven or eight shots were fired and two of them struck Chen, one through the temple and the other through his thigh, while five bullet holes were later discovered on the couch where he had been lying.

Utter confusion was reigning when police officials from Bubbling Well Road station arrived on the scene just before 7.30 p.m. in response to an urgent call from the Chen household, but little information could be obtained from the seven screaming Chinese women and one frightened Chinese youngster they found in the room where Chen was fatally stricken.

Municipal Police Investigate

After examining the surroundings, Settlement police took nine handcuffed males, Chen's son-in-law, a chauffeur and several members of Chen's bodyguard to Bubbling Well Road for further investigation.

Linking up incoherent statements obtained from eye-witnesses to the assassination, it is believed by the Settlement police that the armed band gained access to the Chen house (see picture) through a lane to the right of the house.

Filtering silently through the maze of lanes which spreads a network over the badland district north of Yu Yuen Road, the group succeeded in completely surrounding the doomed official's home before suddenly attacking and disarming a lone watchman posted at a side gate to the compound.

Walking boldly through a lane to the [■] of the mansion, a group of [■] of the raiders then calmly knocked at the door, rushed the guard who opened it and marched into the sitting room where Chen Lo and his friends were assembled for the New Year [■].

（手写批注：free C...）
pages.zh:
《字林西报》
1939年2月21日
（印：SA ... N ... 68180 ...）

子弹夺命
击倒伪政权部长
于上海寓所

来自恶地之袭击者
成为新年庆典中
冷酷的不速之客

日本宪兵
调查此案

陈籙卫兵束手无策
枪手制造混乱吓退宾客

南京政权伪“外交部长”陈籙，周日晚在其寓所——愚园路668弄25号——迎来了死神，当时六名武装男子强行闯入其客厅，在该官员慵懒地躺在沙发上时向其开枪。

现场共发射七八发子弹，其中两发击中陈籙，一发穿过太阳穴，另一发穿过大腿，而在他躺卧的沙发上后来发现了五个弹孔。

当静安寺路警察局的警官接到陈家紧急呼叫并于晚上7点30分前赶到现场时，屋内一片混乱，但从他们发现的七名尖叫的中国妇女和一名受惊的中国孩童那里，几乎无法获得任何信息，陈籙正是在此房间受致命伤。

工部局警察展开调查

在检查周围环境后，租界警察将九名戴手铐的男子（包括陈籙的女婿、一名司机和几名陈籙的保镖）带往静安寺路作进一步调查。

结合从刺杀目击者那里获得的支离破碎的陈述，租界警察认为，武装团伙是通过房屋右侧的一条弄堂进入陈宅的（见图）。

这群人无声地穿行于愚园路以北恶地区域纵横交错的弄堂迷宫中，成功在突然发动袭击并解除一名守在侧门的单独看守的武装之前，完全包围了这位注定遇难官员的住所。

一群袭击者大胆地穿过豪宅[■]侧的弄堂，冷静地敲门，冲垮开门的守卫，大步走进客厅，当时陈籙和他的朋友们正聚集在此庆祝新年[■]。

（手写批注：free C...）

pages.en:
Guests Threatened
Petrified by the grim threat of
mausers, the several guests saw the
gangsters coldly pour a stream of
lead into Chen, who crumpled near
his own table with two bullet holes
in his body, one in the head and
one in his thigh.
The gangsters completed their
mission in silence and then,
threatening the guests with death
if an alarm were raised, one of them
flung two leaflets about the room,
while the rest took up positions to
cover the retreat.
Less than a minute after the last
shot had been fired, the lane was
again deserted.
One of the servants who was in
the room when the armed mob
burst through the door told THE
CHINA PRESS yesterday that the
shooting took place so swiftly that
the terrified guests hardly under-
stood what had happened until they
saw their host lying semi-conscious
on the floor, with blood pouring
from two wounds.
Guards Taken By Surprise
It was more than five minutes
before one of the guests recovered
sufficiently to send an alarm
through to Bubbling Well Road
police station, by which time there
was no trace of the gangsters to
be found.
There were many armed guards
in the house when the bandits
entered, the servant related, but
none of them was able to do any-
thing, as the raiders threatened to
shoot at the first sign of anyone
attempting to move. The servant
could not say whether any of the
guards had gone off with the raiders.
When the Settlement police arriv-
ed at Chen's house, they discovered
that the fatally wounded man had
already been removed by members
of his family to the Chinese Red
Cross Hospital. He was taken there
by private car, the police were told,
and on arrival there he was found
to be dead.
Raiders Well Informed
It was later revealed that the
raiders must have been well-inform-
ed of Chen's arrangements for the
night, as they attacked at a time
when most of the armed guards and
watchmen were being entertained by
the master of the house to a New
Year feast.
Throughout yesterday and last
night, the house was being closely
guarded by uniformed and plain-
clothes men attached to the "Ta
Tao" police authorities, who refused
to permit anyone to approach.
Chen's body was removed yester-
day from the Chinese Red Cross
Hospital to the parlors of the Inter-
national Funeral Directors.
It could not be confirmed yester-
day that the sister of Chang Hsieh-
liang, and her husband, were in the
house at the time of the shooting,
but according to information obtain-
ed by THE CHINA PRESS, a large
number of Chinese guests were in
the house when Chen was shot.
pages.zh:
宾客受威胁
在毛瑟枪冷酷的威胁下吓得呆若木鸡，几位宾客眼睁睁看着匪徒冷静地向陈籙倾泻弹雨，陈籙瘫倒在自己的桌子旁，身上有两个弹孔，一个在头部，一个在大腿。
匪徒无声地完成了任务，然后威胁宾客若发出警报即予射杀，其中一人在房间内抛撒了两张传单，其余人则占据位置掩护撤退。
最后一声枪响后不到一分钟，弄堂再次空无一人。
一名当时在武装暴徒破门而入时身处屋内的仆人昨日告诉《字林西报》，射击发生得如此迅速，以至于惊恐的宾客直到看见主人半昏迷地躺在地上，两处伤口鲜血直流时，才明白发生了什么事。
卫兵措手不及
据该仆人叙述，过了五分多钟，才有一位宾客恢复过来，足以向静安寺路警察局发出警报，而到那时，已找不到匪徒的任何踪迹。
仆人称，匪徒进入时屋内有许多武装卫兵，但无人能采取任何行动，因为袭击者威胁说，任何人只要有试图移动的迹象就会立即开枪。该仆人无法说明是否有卫兵随匪徒离去。
当租界警察到达陈宅时，发现这名受致命伤的人已被其家属送往中国红十字会医院。警方获悉，他是被私家车送往那里的，到达时被发现已经死亡。
袭击者消息灵通
后来的情况显示，袭击者一定对陈籙当晚的安排知之甚详，因为他们发动袭击时，大多数武装卫兵和看守正接受家主款待，参加新年宴会。
昨天全天及昨晚，该住宅一直由隶属于“大道”警察当局的身着制服和便衣的人员严密把守，他们拒绝任何人靠近。
陈籙的遗体昨日从中国红十字会医院移至国际殡仪馆的礼堂。
昨日无法证实张学良的姐姐及其姐夫在枪击发生时是否在屋内，但据《字林西报》获得的消息，陈籙被枪击时，屋内有大量中国宾客。

pages.en:
Chen Lo's Career
Chen Lo was born at Foochow,
Fukien, in 1878; and after studying
languages and law at the Foochow
Arsenal School, was sent to France,
where he graduated from Paris Uni-
versity, LL.B., in 1903.
After touring several countries as
a member of the Ching Imperial
Commission of investigation into
occidental government schemes be-
tween 1906 and 1907, he accom-
panied the Chinese Delegation to
the Hague Conference as a second-
class secretary of the Imperial
Embassy. In 1908 he was made an
advisor to the Chinese Foreign
Office.
During 1909 Chen served as direc-
tor of political affairs, and from
1910 to the end of 1911, after the
establishment of the Republic, he
was appointed Envoy Extraordinary
and Minister Plenipotentiary to the
Republic of Mexico, which post
held until the outbreak of
world war in 1914.
Chen was then made Minister
Plenipotentiary to the Sino-Rus-
sian-Mongolian Conference at
Kiakta in 1914 and the following
year was appointed Resident-Gen-
eral at Urga. After remaining at
that post for two years, Chen was
made vice-Minister for Foreign
Affairs from 1918 to 1920. He was
Minister to France from 1920 to 1927
and in 1923 was Chinese Delegate
to the League of Nations.
From then onwards, Chen was
engaged in private legal practice in
Shanghai, but in 1934, was asked to
become an advisor to the Ministry
of Foreign Affairs.
At the fall of Nanking in 1937,
he disappeared from political acti-
vity, to re-emerge as a member of
the puppet regime formed in Nan-
king last year.
pages.zh:
陈籙生平
陈籙于1878年出生于福建福州；在福州船政学堂学习语言和法律后，被派往法国，并于1903年毕业于巴黎大学，获法学学士学位。
1906年至1907年间，作为清廷考察西洋政治制度特派团成员游历数国后，他作为大清帝国公使馆二等秘书陪同中国代表团参加海牙会议。1908年，他被任命为中国外务部顾问。
1909年，陈籙担任政事局局长，1910年至1911年底，民国成立后，他被任命为驻墨西哥共和国特命全权公使，该职位一直担任至1914年第一次世界大战爆发。
随后，陈籙于1914年被任命为恰克图中俄蒙会议全权公使，次年又被任命为库伦驻札大臣。在该职位任职两年后，陈籙于1918年至1920年担任外交部次长。1920年至1927年任驻法公使，并于1923年担任中国出席国际联盟代表。
此后，陈籙在上海从事私人法律执业，但在1934年，受邀担任外交部顾问。
1937年南京沦陷时，他退出政治活动，直至去年作为在南京成立的伪政权成员重新出现。

pages.en:
NORTH CHINA DAILY NEWS
FEB 21 1939
No. S. P. ( )
Date ____

Chen Loh, Foreign Minister
Of “Reformed” Rule Killed

Large Gang Enters House Off Yu Yuen Road ;
Victim Riddled ; Patriotic Papers Left

BY far the most important assassination on patriotic grounds effected in Shanghai since the 1937 hostilities was carried out on Sunday evening when Mr. Chen Loh, Foreign Minister of the “Reformed Government” and a former Chinese Minister to France, was riddled with bullets in his residence, No. 25, Lane 668 Yu Yuen Road, in territory under Japanese control.

The “China New Year” assassination, which was apparently executed according to carefully laid plans, was performed at about 7 o’clock by a large gang of alleged political agents who acted with speed and precision and escaped easily despite the presence of a number of Mr. Chen’s bodyguards. Two of the latter disappeared with the assassins.

Some fifteen men were in the group that went to Mr. Chen’s residence, seized and disarmed the watchman at the front gate and then went to the rear door. About half of these men entered the house and walked to the dining-room on the ground floor where Mr. Chen was sitting with members of his family and one or two guests. They pointed pistols at the “Reformed Government” official and fired a number of times. One of the bullets went through his head and another penetrated his right leg. He slumped back on the sofa where he was seated and died almost instantly.

“All Finished!”

The intruders did not leave immediately but stayed in the rooms on the ground floor for several minutes. Before they departed, in a body, one of them exclaimed in the Northern dialect of Chinese: “It is all finished!” Then they marched out, nonchalantly. They found no difficulty in escaping into Japanese-controlled territory. As soon as they were gone the terrified relatives of Mr. Chen telephoned for a Shanghai Fire Brigade ambulance. He was taken to the Chinese Red Cross Hospital in Avenue Haig but was dead when admitted.

Two of the armed men attached to the late official’s household were not to be found after the shooting, and it was believed they had left with the gang, either willingly or under threat.

The pistols used by the intruders were of .32 and .38 calibre. It was later determined by arms experts that one of the weapons, a .38, had been responsible for the assassination of Mr. Chien Hua on February 6. Mr. Chien, who was a sub-editor of the Chinese daily “Shun Pao” and member of the Japanese newspaper censorship board, was shot in Race Course Road, near Yu Ya Ching Road, in broad daylight while he was riding in a rickshaw en route to the “Shun Pao” offices.

Pamphlets at Victim’s Side

As in several recent assassinations of “Reformed Government” officials, pro-Chinese-Government pamphlets were left by the perpetrators before they fled the scene. These papers, which were found on the blood-soaked, bullet-riddled sofa where Mr. Chen met his death, contained slogans supporting the National Government and Gen. Chiang Kai-shek, and denouncing “traitors.”

（手写批注：Lio C?）
pages.zh:
《字林西报》
1939年2月21日
编号 S. P. ( )
日期 ____

“维新”政府外交部长陈箓遇刺身亡

大帮歹徒闯入愚园路旁宅邸；
受害者身中数弹；现场留下爱国刊物

自1937年战事爆发以来，上海发生的基于爱国动机的暗杀事件中，最为重要的一起发生于周日晚间。当时，“维新政府”外交部长、前中国驻法公使陈箓先生，在其位于日军控制区愚园路668弄25号的寓所内被乱枪射杀。

这起“中国新年”暗杀案显然是经过周密策划后执行的，大约在7点钟，由一大群疑似政治特工的人员实施。这伙人行动迅速精准，尽管陈箓先生有多名保镖在场，他们仍轻易逃脱。其中两名保镖随刺客一同失踪。

前往陈箓先生寓所的团伙约有十五人，他们在大门口制服并缴了守门人的械，随后绕至后门。其中约半数人进入屋内，走到底层的餐厅，陈箓先生当时正与家人及一两位客人在此就座。他们用枪指着这位“维新政府”官员，连开数枪。一颗子弹穿过他的头部，另一颗击中其右腿。他向后瘫倒在他所坐的沙发上，几乎立即死亡。

“全完了！”

入侵者并未立即离开，而是在底层的房间里停留了几分钟。在他们集体离去之前，其中一人用中国北方方言喊道：“全完了！”随后，他们若无其事地大步走出。他们毫无困难地逃入了日军控制区。他们一走，陈箓先生惊恐的亲属便打电话呼叫上海救火会救护车。他被送往海格路（Avenue Haig）的中国红十字会医院，但入院时已死亡。

枪击发生后，人们发现该已故官员家中的两名武装人员不见踪影，据信他们是自愿或受胁迫随那伙人离开的。

入侵者使用的手枪口径为.32和.38。后经武器专家鉴定，其中一支.38口径的手枪曾用于2月6日钱华（Chien Hua）先生的暗杀案。钱华先生是中文日报《申报》的副编辑，也是日本新闻审查委员会成员。他在白天乘坐人力车前往《申报》馆途中，在跑马厅路（Race Course Road）靠近虞洽卿路（Yu Ya Ching Road）处遭枪击。

受害者身旁的传单

与近期几起针对“维新政府”官员的暗杀案一样，行凶者在逃离现场前留下了亲中国政府的小册子。这些文件是在陈箓先生遇害时所在的血迹斑斑、弹孔累累的沙发上发现的，内容包含支持国民政府和蒋介石将军以及谴责“汉奸”的口号。

（手写批注：Lio C?）

The late Mr. Chen was 61 years old,
a native of Foochow. In his youth
was sent to France where he
studied at the University of Paris.
He received a law degree in Paris
in 1906. The following year or so he
spent in touring Europe and America
studying systems of government. He
was a member of the Chinese Im-
perial Embassy to The Hague in 1907.
After some years in the Ministry of
Foreign Affairs at home he was sent
by the Republican Government as
Minister to Mexico in 1914. Mr. Chen
became Chinese Plenipotentiary to
the Sino-Russo-Mongolian Conference
at Kiakta the same year. From 1915
to 1917 he was Resident-General at
Urga, and in 1918 he became Vice
Minister of Foreign Affairs. He was
Chinese Minister to France from
1920 to 1927, and acted as Chinese
Delegate to the League of Nations in
1923. In 1932 Mr. Chen entered pri-
vate law practice in Shanghai. He
was attached to the Ministry of For-
eign Affairs as adviser from 1934 with
residence at Nanking.

Japanese Make Arrest

Japanese Military Police, while
raiding houses off Jessfield Road in
Extra-Settlement territory yesterday
morning, are reported to have ar-
rested one Chinese, but it could not
be ascertained last night whether the
arrest had any bearing on the murder
of Mr. Chen Loh. The lane in which
Mr. Chen's house is situated and
where he was killed leads from a
Municipal road into Japanese-
controlled territory and is not
patrolled by the Settlement Police.

Foreign Authorities Accused

Tokyo, Feb. 19.
The Japanese newspapers are giving
prominence to what they describe as
"the daily terroristic demonstrations
staged in the International Settle-
ment and the French Concession at
Shanghai, whose victims are officials
of the new Nanking government or
Chinese dealing with Japanese."
The demonstrators are alleged to
be "hired agents of the Kuomintang
Government who, with bases in the
Settlement and the Concession, are
freely carrying on their anti-Japan-
ese operations."
The Shanghai correspondent of the
"Hochi" reports that over two dozen
cases of terroristic demonstrations
have occurred in the International
Settlement and the French Concession
in the past ten days, but all the per-
petrators are at large."
He goes on to describe the Japanese
representations to the Shanghai
Municipal Council as "timely," but
says he is sceptical concerning the
Chairman's reply, which he is "in-
clined to regard as a matter of
courtesy."
"Opinion is gaining strength in
Japanese officialdom in Shanghai," the
correspondent continues, "that the
bases of operations of the Chinese
terrorists in the International Settle-
ment and the French Concession
should be raided by the Japanese in
case the foreign authorities fail to
demonstrate their ability to control
them effectively."—Reuter.

Japanese Army Concerned

Nanking, Feb. 20.
Terrorist acts in Shanghai, parti-
cularly the assassination of Mr. Chen
Lo, Foreign Minister of the "Reform-
ed Government," were arousing
"grave concern" among Japanese
military authorities, a spokesman of
the Japanese Expeditionary Force to
Central China declared here today.
"It is extremely regrettable," the
spokesman said: "that terrorist acts
have occurred repeatedly in the
International Settlement and French
Concession in Shanghai in striking
contrast with the peaceful conditions
which are being maintained in Japan-
ese occupied zones."—Domei.

已故陈箓先生享年61岁，
福州人。年轻时被派往法国，
在巴黎大学求学。他于1906年
在巴黎获得法学学位。随后大约一年时间，
他游历欧美，研究各国政府体制。
1907年，他是中国驻海牙公使馆的成员。
在国内外交部任职数年后，
他于1914年被共和政府任命为
驻墨西哥公使。同年，陈箓先生成为
中俄蒙恰克图会议的中国全权代表。
1915年至1917年，他担任库伦（Urga）办事大员，
1918年出任外交部次长。
1920年至1927年，他担任中国驻法公使，
并于1923年担任中国出席国际联盟的代表。
1932年，陈箓先生在上海从事私人律师业务。
自1934年起，他以顾问身份隶属外交部，
居住于南京。

日方实施逮捕

据报道，日本宪兵队昨天上午在越界筑路区域极司菲尔路（Jessfield Road）旁的住宅进行搜查时，逮捕了一名中国人，但截至昨晚尚无法确定此次逮捕是否与陈箓先生被杀案有关。陈箓先生寓所所在且其遇害的那条弄堂，从一条工部局道路通向日军控制区，并不由租界警察巡逻。

指责外国当局

东京，2月19日。
日本报纸显著报道了他们所称的
“在上海公共租界和法租界每日上演的恐怖示威活动，
其受害者是新南京政府的官员或与日本人打交道的中国人。”
据称，这些示威者是“国民党政府雇佣的特工，
他们以租界和法租界为基地，自由地进行反日活动。”
《报知新闻》（Hochi）的上海记者报道说，
过去十天里，公共租界和法租界发生了二十多起恐怖示威案件，
但所有肇事者均在逃。”
他接着将日本方面向上海公共租界工部局提出的交涉描述为“及时的”，
但他对董事会主席的答复表示怀疑，
他“倾向于认为这只是一种礼节性的回应。”
该记者继续写道：“上海日本官方人士中日益强烈的意见认为，
如果外国当局不能证明其有能力有效控制，
日军应突袭公共租界和法租界内的中国恐怖分子行动基地。”——路透社。

日军表示关切

南京，2月20日。
华中派遣军发言人今日在此宣布，
上海的恐怖行为，特别是“维新政府”外交部长陈箓（Chen Lo）先生遇刺案，
引起了日本军方的“严重关切”。
该发言人称：“令人极为遗憾的是，
与日军占领区维持的和平状况形成鲜明对比的是，
上海公共租界和法租界内反复发生恐怖行为。”——同盟社。

SHANGHAI TIMES.
FEB 21 1939

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. M. P. REG. & PHY. 9
No. S. R. D. _________
Dc

Chen Loh, Minister Of
Reformed Government Is
Assassinated On Sunday

Veteran Statesman Shot In Own Residence Off
Yu Yuen Road Before Terrified Family;
Bodyguard Disappears With Gunmen

JAPANESE PARTY FIRED UPON BY
LONE GUNMAN ON NANKING RD.

Twenty-seven hours after his secret arrival from Nanking, to celebrate the Lunar New Year Holidays with his family and relatives in Shanghai, Mr. Chen Loh, 61-year-old Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Reformed Government of Nanking, was assassinated at about seven o'clock on Sunday evening at his residence at House 25, Lane 668, Yu Yuen Road, while preparing to partake of New Year dinner.

The veteran statesman, who served as Minister to France and to Mexico, under the old Peking Government and was Vice-Chairman of the Treaty Commission of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the National Government, since May, 1938, was killed by a group of about eight gunmen, who broke into his guest room and fired a volley of shots at him, after one of them had shouted, "All is finished," and told the other members of the family that no harm would come to them.

After the departure of the assassins, self-styled the "Chinese Youth Iron and Blood Army," it was discovered that the only body-guard, who was on duty outside the residence of the murdered politician, had disappeared. It was reported that he had been surprised by the killers and disarmed. It was further alleged that he had left with the terrorists without being forced and a suspicion has arisen that perhaps he had arranged it so that when the terrorists arrived, no one but himself would be on guard.

Japanese Attacked

The assassination of Mr. Chen Loh, which is the most important political killing to have been staged in Shanghai in recent months, was not the only terrorist activity on Sunday. Although Mr. Chen Loh was killed in territory coming under the jurisdiction of the Japanese-sponsored City Government, two outrages were staged in the Settlement.

At about 3 o'clock in the afternoon shots rang out along the crowded Nanking Road, outside the Kwan Sung Yuen Restaurant, near the corner of Fokien Road. Pandemonium reigned and it was finally ascertained that a group of Japanese, including an Army photographer man and two women, were fired upon by an unidentified Chinese gunman, just as they had stepped into a taxicab, after having partaken of a Chinese tiffin. The photographer was injured in the arm, one woman was hit in the chest and ribs, while the second man received a slight wound of the wrist. The gunman managed to escape following a gun-battle with the police.

The last event of the New Year's Day was the hurling of a hand-grenade into the compound of the Toyota Cotton Mill on Singapore Road at about 11.30 a.m. Nobody was injured and very little damage was done.

（右侧手写批注：）

《上海泰晤士报》
1939年2月21日

上海公共租界工部局警务处
S. M. P. 注册与体检科 9
编号 S. R. D. _________
Dc

维新政府部长陈箓
周日遇刺

资深政治家在愚园路旁自家寓所内、惊恐的家人面前遭枪击；
保镖随枪手消失

一名孤身枪手在南京路向日方人员开枪

南京“维新政府”61岁的外交部长陈箓先生，在秘密抵达上海27小时后，正准备与家人亲戚共度农历新年假期。周日晚7时许，他在愚园路668弄25号寓所准备享用年夜饭时遇刺身亡。

这位资深政治家曾在旧北京政府时期担任驻法国和墨西哥公使，并自1938年5月起担任国民政府外交部条约委员会副委员长。他被一群约八名枪手杀害，这伙人闯入他的客房，其中一人高喊“全完了”，并告知其他家庭成员不会伤害他们，随后向他扫射了一排子弹。

刺客自称“中国青年铁血军”离去后，人们发现当时在遇刺政治家寓所外执勤的唯一一名保镖已经失踪。据报道，他被杀手出其不意地制服并缴械。另有说法称，他是未经强迫便随恐怖分子离开的，因此有人怀疑也许是他安排了当恐怖分子到达时，只有他自己在岗。

日本人遇袭

陈箓先生遇刺案是近几个月来上海发生的最重要的政治谋杀案，但这并非周日唯一的恐怖活动。虽然陈箓先生是在日本扶持的市政府管辖区域内被杀，但租界内也发生了两起暴行。

下午3点左右，拥挤的南京路上福建路路口附近的冠生园酒楼外响起枪声。现场一片混乱，最终查明，一群日本人（包括一名陆军摄影师和两名妇女）在用完中式午餐后，刚踏进一辆出租车时，遭到一名身份不明的中国枪手射击。摄影师手臂受伤，一名妇女胸部和肋骨中弹，另一名男子手腕受轻伤。枪手在与警察交火后成功逃脱。

新年当天的最后一件事是上午11点30分左右，有人向新加坡路（Singapore Road）丰田棉纺厂厂区投掷了一枚手榴弹。无人受伤，损失甚微。

（右侧手写批注：）

01880

Large Band
Investigation conducted following the murder of Mr. Chen Loh, revealed that a band of about 15 Chinese approached his residence in a lane off the Settlement road, at shortly after 7 o'clock on Sunday evening, overpowered and disarmed the only bodyguard on duty, who subsequently disappeared with them, and then gained entry into the residence, after being admitted by an amah.
Only eight of the group went into the house, while the others spread around the house to keep watch. The killers surprised Mr. Chen Loh, members of his family and guests, among whom, it is reported, was his daughter-in-law sister of the "Young Marshal" Chang Hsuch-liang and daughter of the late Marshal Chang Tso-lin, in the guest room.
Before the surprised family could make a move or scream, after being covered with eight Mausers and other pistols, the leader of the assassins said, "All is finished," and then a staccato of pistol fire was heard and Mr. Chen Loh slumped on the sofa where he was sitting, while blood rushed from the wounds, two of which were in the head. The terrorists fled immediately and by the time the City Government Police, Japanese Gendarmerie and Settlement Police had arrived on the scene, there was no sign of them except the empty cartridge cases.
An ambulance conveyed Mr. Chen Loh to the Red Cross Hospital on Avenue Haig, where he died soon after. No funeral arrangements have as yet been announced. Upon decamping the assassins scattered leaflets on which various slogans, such as "Exterminate traitors," were printed.

Born In Foochow
Mr. Chen Loh was born in Foochow in 1878. He received his LL.B. in Paris and was a Hanlin Scholar and compiler of Imperial Examinations. His first diplomatic appointment was in 1914, when he became Minister to Mexico under the Peking regime. In 1918-19 he served as Vice-Minister of Foreign Affairs and the following year was appointed Minister to France, which post he held until 1923. Since his return to China he was Adviser and Vice-Chairman of the Treaty Commission of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
The deceased's eldest son, Mr Chen Yu-tao, who is serving as Director of General Affairs of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Reformed Government, directly under his father, was not in Shanghai when the assassination took place.

Eight Arrests Made
Eight male Chinese were placed under arrest by Japanese gendarmerie following a house-to-house search at about 9:45 a.m. yesterday in Erh Kang Li and Hsing Shen Li of Jessfield Road in the Zaokadoo District. The arrests were presumably in connection with the assassination of Mr. Chen Loh.
No confirmation of this, however, could be obtained yesterday, and no explanation for the arrests was learnt to have been made.
Shortly before 9 o'clock yesterday morning two Japanese gendarmes, accompanied by over 30 Chinese police of the Shanghai City Government, proceeded to the lanes in question and made a thorough search of the houses.
pages.zh:
01880

大型帮派
对陈箓先生谋杀案进行的调查显示，周日晚7点刚过，一伙约15名中国人接近位于租界道路旁弄堂内的其寓所，制服并缴械了当时唯一在岗的保镖，该保镖随后随他们一同消失，之后由一名阿妈（女佣）开门，这伙人得以进入寓所。
该团伙中只有八人进入屋内，其余人则分散在房屋周围放哨。凶手在客房内突袭了陈箓先生、其家人及宾客，据报宾客中包括“少帅”张学良的弟媳、已故大元帅张作霖的女儿。
在受惊的家人来得及做出反应或呼救之前，在被八支毛瑟枪及其他手枪指住后，刺客头目说道：“一切都结束了”，随即听到一阵急促的枪声，陈箓先生瘫倒在他所坐的沙发上，伤口鲜血涌出，其中两处位于头部。恐怖分子立即逃窜，待市政府警察、日本宪兵队及租界警察抵达现场时，除空弹壳外，已无他们的踪迹。
救护车将陈箓先生送往海格大道（Avenue Haig）的红十字会医院，他不久后身亡。目前尚未公布葬礼安排。刺客在撤离时散发了印有“铲除汉奸”等各种标语的传单。

生于福州
陈箓先生于1878年生于福州。他在巴黎获得法学学士学位，曾是翰林院编修及会试同考官。他的首个外交任命是在1914年，当时他在北京政府治下出任驻墨西哥公使。1918-19年间，他担任外交部次长，次年被任命为驻法国公使，该职位他一直担任至1923年。自返回中国以来，他担任外交部条约委员会顾问兼副委员长。
死者的长子陈佑道先生，现任维新政府外交部总务司司长，直接在其父麾下任职，刺杀发生时他不在上海。

逮捕八人
昨天上午9点45分左右，日本宪兵队在曹家渡区极司菲尔路（Jessfield Road）的二康里和兴神里进行逐户搜查后，拘留了八名中国男子。这些逮捕行动据信与陈箓先生遇刺案有关。
然而，昨天未能获得对此事的确认，也未获悉关于逮捕原因的任何解释。
昨天上午9点前不久，两名日本宪兵在上海市政府30多名中国警察的陪同下，前往上述弄堂，并对房屋进行了彻底搜查。

pages.en:
One of the men taken by the gendarmerie was Loh Peng-kiang, 30, said to be a silk merchant; two others, Mou Lai-kan and Sze Tsai-lang—are reported to be owners of an eating house in the Western district. The others, whose occupation is unknown, are Tsai Ting-kang, age 24, Tsai Ting-chen, age 19, and one other man and two other Chinese youths.
The party were ordered into a Japanese military truck, it was stated, and speeded away to an unknown direction.
It could not be learnt whether the arrested men had any connection with the shooting yesterday morning, or whether any incriminating evidence against them had been found for the arrest.

Attack On Japanese

Striking in broad daylight in the congested Nanking Road district, an unidentified Chinese terrorist on Sunday afternoon seriously injured two Japanese.
Wounded in the right upper arm, while sitting in a taxicab, was Mr. J. Koyanagi, official Japanese Army photographer. Miss M. Morioka, who with another Japanese woman and another man, were also in the taxicab narrowly missed death when one of the assailant's bullets penetrated her right chest, glanced off a rib and emerged from her left side. Her heart and lungs were not touched. Also wounded was Mr. Rokuro Sato who suffered a flesh injury in the right wrist. The fourth member of the party escaped unscathed. A Chinese beggar was hit in the right leg, by a stray bullet during the chase for the gunman staged by Settlement police.
The attack occurred in front of the Kwan Sung Yuen Chinese restaurant, 445-53 Nanking Road at about 2.40 p.m. A Chinese was recently shot and killed at the same restaurant allegedly by anti-Japanese elements.
The party of four, two men and two women, had finished lunch at the restaurant when they summoned a taxicab. The vehicle, an antiquated model, was not provided by any of the major taxicab companies. As the taxi was about to start, with its four passengers, a slight man in Chinese clothes stepped up and began shooting at random into the car through an open window.
Sitting next to the driver Mr. Koyanagi was hit in the right upper arm, the bullet shattering the bone. Hit in the chest, Miss Morioka, who was in the back seat with two others, slumped back unconscious.
The taxicab driver allegedly fled immediately after the assault.
The injured were taken in a Fire Brigade ambulance to the Fountin Hospital, N. Szechuen Road, where they were detained.
Mr. Koyanagi as official photographer covered the Hsuchow and Hankow campaigns of the Japanese Army. He never was wounded. He returned to Shanghai early this month after spending some time in Japan.

Police Chase

The gunman, who fired at the Japanese, and his alleged accomplice, were chased down an alleyway, right up to Kiukiang Road, by two Chinese constables of the Shanghai Municipal Police, who fired four shots at the assailants, but without result. A Sikh Havildar also joined in the chase.
pages.zh:
被宪兵队带走的人中有一名是罗彭江（Loh Peng-kiang，音译），30岁，据称是一名丝绸商人；另外两人，牟来根（Mou Lai-kan，音译）和施再郎（Sze Tsai-lang，音译），据报是西区一家餐馆的老板。其他人职业不明，分别是蔡廷康（Tsai Ting-kang，音译），24岁，蔡廷臣（Tsai Ting-chen，音译），19岁，以及另一名男子和两名中国青年。
据称，这些人被命令登上一辆日本军用卡车，迅速驶向一个未知的方向。
目前无法得知被捕者是否与昨天上午的枪击案有关，或者是否发现了足以证明其有罪并导致逮捕的证据。

袭击日本人

周日午后，在拥挤的南京路地区，一名身份不明的中国恐怖分子在大白天行凶，致使两名日本人重伤。
日本陆军官方摄影师小柳（J. Koyanagi，音译）先生坐在出租车内时，右臂上部受伤。森冈（M. Morioka，音译）小姐与另一名日本女子及一名男子同在出租车内，当袭击者的一颗子弹穿透她的右胸，擦过肋骨并从左侧穿出时，她险些丧命。她的心脏和肺部未受损伤。同样受伤的还有佐藤六郎（Rokuro Sato，音译）先生，其右手腕受皮肉伤。同行的第四人毫发无损。在租界警察追捕枪手期间，一名中国乞丐被流弹击中右腿。
袭击发生在下午2点40分左右，地点为南京路445-53号的冠生园中餐馆门前。最近，一名中国人在同一家餐馆被枪杀，据称系反日分子所为。
这两男两女一行四人在餐馆用完午餐后叫了一辆出租车。该车车型老旧，并非由任何主要出租车公司提供。当出租车载着四名乘客即将启动时，一名身穿中式服装的瘦小男子走上前，透过敞开的车窗向车内随意开枪。
坐在司机旁边的小柳先生右臂上部中弹，骨头碎裂。坐在后座与其他两人在一起的森冈小姐胸部中弹，向后倒下失去知觉。
据称，出租车司机在袭击后立即逃离。
伤者由消防队救护车送往北四川路的福民医院（Fountin Hospital，音译），并在那里留院治疗。
小柳先生作为官方摄影师，曾报道日本陆军在徐州和汉口的战役。他此前从未受伤。他在日本逗留一段时间后，于本月初返回上海。

警方追捕

向日本人开枪的枪手及其 alleged 同伙被两名上海公共租界工部局警务处的中国巡捕沿一条小巷一直追到九江路，巡捕向袭击者开了四枪，但未击中。一名锡克教警长也加入了追捕。

CRIME BR NCH
C. I. Misc. No. 38/39.    MAY 15,    39.

FURTHER TO LETTER TO JAPANESE GENDARMERIE.

At 12 noon 12.5.39 S. Inspt. Darters on
Charge Room duty, Central Station, communicated
to the undersigned by phone the fact that a
few moments previous prisoner Lau Foh Sang
(呂富生) detained therein on behalf of the
Japanese authorities since the 16.3.39, had
attempted suicide in his cell by hanging.

Enquiries revealed that this man had torn
a strip of cloth from his long gown and tying
same round his throat had attached the other
end to the cell bars, but in jumping to the
ground the cloth had broken, and that he beyond
hanging suffered a slight bruise of the head
and suffered no other injury, and in view of
this he was not sent to hospital.

On the morning of 15.5.39, the undersigned
removed this prisoner from the cells and from
the ensuing conversation formed the opinion
that this man is at present slightly mentally
un-balanced, in view of which, it is recommended
that he be medically examined and if necessary
detained in Hospital pending a satisfactory
conclusion being reached in this case.

刑事科
刑事情报杂项第 38/39 号。    1939年5月15日。

致日本宪兵队信函之后续。

1939年5月12日中午12时，中央车站值班室的达特斯（Darters，音译）高级督察通过电话告知下文签署人，此前代表日本当局于1939年3月16日拘留于此的囚犯吕富生（Lau Foh Sang），曾在其牢房内试图上吊自杀。

经查，此人从长衫上撕下一条布条，一端系在脖子上，另一端系在牢房栏杆上，但在跳向地面时布条断裂，因此除了勒痕外，他头部仅有轻微挫伤，无其他伤害，鉴于此，他未被送往医院。

1939年5月15日上午，下文签署人将该囚犯从牢房提出，并通过随后的谈话认为，此人目前精神略有不稳，鉴于此，建议对其进行医学检查，如有必要，在本案得出满意结论之前将其拘押在医院。

A male Chinese person named Zee Ah Ming

1939年4月10日，日本宪兵队同意释放邓海大（Dung Hai Dah），回想起来，他于1939年3月16日在贵州路与一名嫌疑刺客邵福生（Zau Foo Sung，音译）一同被捕，日本宪兵队未能找到足以证明需继续拘留他的证据。

REGISTRY
H. No. 9059
March 26, 39.

ASSISTANCE TO JAPANESE MILITARY POLICE HEADQUARTERS

D.S.I. Crighton                                      C.D.I. Crabb

In reference to arrest of Keh Tsun Liang
(郭志良) at 6.20 a.m. 25-3-39, at Lane 830, House 28,
Amoy Road, the undersigned having perused his statement
sent for C.D.I. 153 Leh Kang Dee (陸根弟) attached to
Gordon Road Station and he, on being questioned,
admitted having borrowed from Keh the sum of $2,000.00,
but stated that he had done so on behalf of one named
Zau Ngoh Ming (趙鶴鳴), one of the partners in the
Dah Lih (大來) Theatre, and also employed by a
Japanese in Hongkew as an interpreter.

A detailed written statement, in which he
denies ownership of the Dah Lih Theatre, stating that
it is his brother and not he, is herewith attached for
information.

In comparing the written statement of Keh
Tsun Liang and C.D.I. 153, also taking into consideration
that the previously arrested man Zau Foo Sang (邵福生)
during his detention by the S.M. Police has made a
complete denial of the offence in question, it would
appear that the allegations made against these men had
been instigated by the man Zau Ngoh Ming, who is residing
at an unknown Japanese residence in Hongkew and that the
whole case is nothing more or less than a "Frame Up",
however until such time as Zau Foo Sang, who is due to
be returned to Crime Branch Headquarters on the afternoon
of 26-3-39, has been re-questioned, the undersigned
recommends that the case be left in abeyance.

协助日本军方警察总部

副督察长 克里顿（Crighton）                                      刑事调查官 克拉布（Crabb）

关于1939年3月25日上午6点20分在爱多亚路（Amoy Road）830弄28号逮捕郭志良（Keh Tsun Liang）一事，下文签署人查阅了其供词后，传唤了附属于戈登路捕房的刑事调查员153号陆根弟（Leh Kang Dee），经讯问，他承认曾向郭借款2,000.00元，但声称他是代表赵鹤鸣（Zau Ngoh Ming，音译）借的，赵是大来（Dah Lih）剧院的合伙人之一，同时也受雇于虹口的一名日本人担任翻译。

随函附上一份详细的书面陈述供参考，他在其中否认拥有大来剧院，称所有者是其兄弟而非他本人。

对比郭志良和刑事调查员153号的书面陈述，并考虑到此前被捕的邵福生（Zau Foo Sung）在被上海公共租界工部局警务处拘留期间完全否认了相关罪行，看来针对这些人的指控是由居住在虹口某处不为人知的日本住所的赵鹤鸣唆使的，整个案件不过是一起“栽赃陷害”，然而，在定于1939年3月26日下午送回刑事科总部的邵福生接受再次讯问之前，下文签署人建议将此案暂缓处理。

In reference to the documents seized, five
of them definitely connect the man Koh Tseu Liang as
having been in close contact with persons working in the
Nationalist Government, but inasmuch as they are two to
three years old, they do not carry much weight in regard

At 4.50 p.m. 25-3-39, the prisoner Zau Foo
Sung was returned to this office by Sgt. Major Katoda
and at this time it was noticed that he was suffering
from a fairly bad abrasion of the left eye, also
several minor bruises of the body and legs. Questioned
regarding same he stated that on three occasions during
his detention by the Japanese Military Police, he had
been subject to torture.

Re-questioned regarding his allegations
against Koh Tseu Liang, this man made another written
statement in which he emphatically denied that he had in
any way implicated this man in the "Assassination of
Chen Leh". Continuing he explained how he had related
the quarrel between Koh Tseu Liang and Zau Ngoh Ming, and
how on one occasion Koh had jokingly accused him of being
a small traitor. (Translation attached).

Regarding the part in his statement, where he
relates to the meeting of a male Chinese who gave the
name of Mau You Vung (毛友文) of the Shanghai Municipal
Police, such a man exists in the person of D.S.I. Mau
You Vung (毛伊文) 1/c of Chinese detectives, Sinna

关于查获的文件，其中五份确凿地表明郭子良（Koh Tseu Liang，音译，即前文郭志良）与在国民政府工作的人员有密切联系，但由于这些文件已有两三年之久，在本案中分量不大。译文附后。

1939年3月25日下午4点50分，囚犯邵福生（Zau Foo Sung）由军士长片田（Katoda，音译）送回本办公室，此时注意到他左眼有相当严重的擦伤，身体和腿部也有几处轻微瘀伤。就此进行讯问时，他声称在日本军方警察拘留期间，他曾三次遭受酷刑。

就其对郭子良的指控再次进行讯问时，此人又做了一份书面陈述，坚决否认他曾以任何方式牵连郭子良参与“陈箓刺杀案”。他接着解释了他如何讲述郭子良与赵鹤鸣之间的争吵，以及郭曾如何开玩笑地指责他是小汉奸。（译文附后）。

关于其陈述中提到会见一名自称是上海公共租界工部局警务处毛友文（Mau You Vung，音译）的中国男子的部分，确实存在这样一个人，即静安捕房（Sinna Station，音译）华籍侦探主管毛伊文（Mau You Vung）副督察长，

pages.en:
KOH TSOU LIANG (郭志良)
Pootung    xx    D.S.I. Brighton
9 a.m.    25/3/39    Nativ. Gu Zhou Ling

My name is Koh Tsou Liang, age 34, native of Pootung,
k/Unemployed, residing Lane 230, House 88, Amoy Road.
I was born in April 1906, in Shanghai. At this time
my parents were residing on North Chekiang Road, the number I
forget. My father was then employed as No. 1 carpenter in
Arts & Crafts, Bubbling Well Road. My father died 14 years
ago, and at present my mother resides with me at the above
address. I have one sister who is living on Elgin Road,
number forgotten.
At the age of 6 years, I entered a Chinese Primary
School on Tsepoo Road, where I remained for 4 years, after
which I entered the Tung wei (通惠) Middle School, French
Concession, where I stayed until attaining the age of 14 years.
Leaving this school I entered the Chinese Polytechnic School
on Rupoh Road, and after studying there for 6 months, I entered
the Shanghai Municipal School for Chinese on Cunningham Road.
At the age of 17 years I left school to enter the Shanghai
Municipal Fire Brigade as Watchman No. 131. I remained in
this position for nearly two years, when owing to sickness
(red eyes) I was forced to resign. Recovering from my sickness
I obtained a position as telephone operator in the Law Offices
of Mr. Lamberger (?), American, at 62 Kiangse Road, where I
remained for about 6 months, when in order to better myself
I entered the Law Office of Mr. Lamiere (?), French, at 34
Nanking Road, as a clerk. In February 1928, I obtained the
position of Chinese Detective Constable No. 86 in the Nantao
City Police under the Zang Ts Ying (常之英) Regime. In
pages.zh:
郭志良 (KOH TSOU LIANG)
浦东    xx    布莱顿警司 (D.S.I. Brighton)
上午9时    1939年3月25日    籍贯：郭州岭 (Gu Zhou Ling)

我叫郭志良，34岁，浦东人，
职业：失业，住爱多亚路 (Amoy Road) 230弄88号。
我于1906年4月出生于上海。当时
我父母住在浙江北路，门牌号我已忘记。我父亲当时受雇于
静安寺路 (Bubbling Well Road) 的“艺术与工艺”公司 (Arts & Crafts)，担任头号木匠。我父亲于14年前去世，目前我母亲与我同住于上述地址。我有一个姐姐，住在埃尔金路 (Elgin Road)，门牌号已忘记。
6岁时，我进入乍浦路 (Tsepoo Road) 的一所华童小学读书，在那里读了4年，之后进入法租界的通惠中学 (Tung wei Middle School)，一直读到14岁。
离开该校后，我进入茹泼路 (Rupoh Road) 的中华职业学校 (Chinese Polytechnic School)，在那里学习了6个月后，进入康脑脱路 (Cunningham Road) 的上海华童公学 (Shanghai Municipal School for Chinese)。
17岁时，我离校加入上海公共租界救火会，担任第131号更夫。我在这个职位上待了将近两年，后因患病（红眼病）被迫辞职。病愈后，我在江西路62号美国人兰伯杰先生 (Mr. Lamberger, ?) 的律师事务所找到一份电话接线员的工作，在那里待了大约6个月，为了谋求更好的发展，我进入南京路34号法国人拉米埃尔先生 (Mr. Lamiere, ?) 的律师事务所担任职员。1928年2月，我在常之英 (Zang Ts Ying) 政权下的南市警察局获得第86号华探职位。在

pages.en:
- 2 -

October 1925 I was transferred to the Peace Maintenance Corps
under Nyi Wah Ling (嚴槐林). I remained in this job until
March 1927, when owing to the outbreak of hostilities, I
resigned my position and took up residence at the home of my
mother at 1205 Boone Road. I remained unemployed until August
1927, when through the introduction of a friend I obtained the
position of Detective Inspector at Taishing (泰興), Kiangsu, where
I remained for 2 months, when owing to a further outbreak of
hostilities in Kiangsu I was forced to return to Shanghai where I
did various small jobs for the next few years.

In the Spring of 1932, I obtained a position of
Detective Inspector of Nanshan District, where I remained for
over two years. In 1935 I was transferred to Suchow where I
remained until June, when seeing that hostilities between
China and Japan were imminent I resigned and returned to
Shanghai, and took up residence with my mother, wife and four
children. Shortly after my return to Shanghai, I was taken
sick with Hongkong feet, and as I found it difficult to walk
I remained at home for nearly one month. Between the outbreak
of hostilities in Shanghai and now I have been unemployed, and
have been supported by my mother, who at the time of my
father's death inherited a bit of money. This, coupled with
my own savings, has helped us to live fairly comfortable until
now, although at present I am in somewhat straitened
circumstances.

Regarding the allegations made against me by the
man Zan Foo Sing (邵富生) I offer the following information
pages.zh:
- 2 -

1925年10月，我被调至严槐林 (Nyi Wah Ling) 麾下的保卫团 (Peace Maintenance Corps)。我一直从事这份工作直到1927年3月，因战事爆发，我辞去职务，搬到我母亲位于博恩路 (Boone Road) 1205号的家中居住。我一直失业到1927年8月，经朋友介绍，我在江苏泰兴 (Taishing) 获得督察职位，在那里待了2个月，后因江苏战事再次爆发，我被迫返回上海，在接下来的几年里做过各种零工。

1932年春，我获得南山地区督察的职位，在那里待了两年多。1935年，我被调往苏州，一直待到6月，鉴于中日战事迫在眉睫，我辞职返回上海，与母亲、妻子和四个孩子同住。回到上海后不久，我患上脚气病 (Hongkong feet)，因行走困难，我在家休养了近一个月。自上海战事爆发至今，我一直失业，靠母亲供养，母亲在我父亲去世时继承了一笔钱。这笔钱加上我自己的积蓄，帮助我们过得相当舒适，直到目前，尽管我现在处境 somewhat straitened (略显窘迫)。

关于邵富生 (Zan Foo Sing) 对我的指控，我就
我与该人的关系提供以下信息

pages.en:
- 3 -
regarding my connections with this man.
Several years ago I had occasion to visit the Chm
wo (九華) Lodging House, Canton Road, then owned and operated
by ex-C.D.S. Mau Tang Ju (馬長書) and at this time met Zau
Foo Sung who was employed as a tea-boy therein. On this
occasion I had nothing to do with him and I did not meet him
again until under the following circumstances.
In February 1938 a friend of mine named Loh Kung
Dee (嘜根弟), a detective Sergeant employed at Gordon Road
Station of the Shanghai Municipal Police, came to my home
and after explaining that he had a friend named Zau Ngoh Ming
(趙鶴鳴) who had previously been employed in a cotton mill in
Tungtseupoo, and who through the hostilities had lost his job,
was preparing to open a Cotton Broker's Hong in Shanghai for the
purpose of trading in that material between this city and the
interior, however owing to financial difficulties, he could not
carry on. Loh Kung Dee then suggested that I lend him two
thousand dollars, and that together, we, i.e. Zau Ngoh Ming,
he and myself start this company. I agreed to assist him, but
not having the money myself, I borrowed same from two of my
school-mates, whose names I do not wish to disclose, but who
I can produce if necessary. This amount I handed to Loh Kung
Dee, however when I approached him a few days later regarding
the opening of the hong he told me to wait. From then on until
sometime in March I kept on to him regarding the opening of
the Cotton Hong, but he always gave me the excuse that things
had not yet been arranged. A few days later I overheard that
pages.zh:
- 3 -
几年前，我曾去过广东路的九华旅馆 (Chm wo Lodging House)，当时由前华捕头马长书 (Mau Tang Ju) 拥有并经营，在那里我遇到了在此当茶役的赵富生 (Zau Foo Sung)。那次我与他没有交集，直到后来在以下情况下才再次见到他。
1938年2月，我的朋友嘜根弟 (Loh Kung Dee)，一名受雇于上海公共租界警务处戈登路捕房的巡佐，来到我家，解释说他的朋友赵鹤鸣 (Zau Ngoh Ming) 此前在东新浦 (Tungtseupoo) 的一家棉纺厂工作，因战事失业，正打算在上海开设一家棉花经纪行 (Cotton Broker's Hong)，目的是在这座城市与内地之间进行棉花贸易，但由于资金困难，无法维持。嘜根弟随后建议我借给他两千美元，由我们三人，即赵鹤鸣、他和我，共同创办这家公司。我同意协助他，但因我自己没有钱，我向两名同学借了这笔钱，他们的名字我不愿透露，但如有需要我可以让他们出面。我把这笔钱交给了嘜根弟，然而几天后当我向他询问开设经纪行的事宜时，他让我等待。从那时起直到3月的某个时候，我一直向他催促开设棉花经纪行，但他总是以事情尚未安排妥当为借口。几天后，我偶然听到

pages.en:
- 4 -

Loh Kung Dee had no intention of opening a Cotton Hong, but
that he had taken over the lease of the Dah Lih (大來)
Theatre on Kweichow Road in partnership with Lau Ngah Ming,
and that same was then being renovated preparatory to opening.
Hearing this I immediately sought Loh Kung Dee at the Dah Lih
Theatre and threatened him that unless he paid me my money
back I would expose him to his superiors. On this day he gave
me $200.00 of my money and told me that he would pay me back
the balance in monthly instalments. As I did not want any
further trouble with him I agreed to his proposal, however in
collecting the balance I had several rows with him as there
were occasions when he would not pay me. On these occasions
he was invariably assisted in his arguments by Lau Foo Sung,
who had obtained a job therein as a ticket collector, also Lau
Ngah Ming. Up to the present Loh Kung Dee still owes me
$55.00, which I have so far failed to collect.

About 6 months ago Lau Foo Sung came to live next
door to me and one day in the passing he happened to mention
to me that he had obtained a position as bodyguard to Mr. Chen
Loh (陳籟). I admit that on this occasion I teased him
about working for traitors, but beyond that I have had nothing
to do with this man, nor have I ever lent him a single dollar.

Regarding his allegations that it was on a certain
day in August 1938, that he met me outside the New World on
Yu Ya Ching Road, I would like to point out that between the
end of July and the beginning of October 1938 I was bedridden
with a very serious attack of blood poisoning and that during
pages.zh:
- 4 -

嘜根弟无意开设棉花经纪行，而是与刘阿明 (Lau Ngah Ming) 合伙接手了贵州路大来戏院 (Dah Lih Theatre) 的租赁权，当时正在进行装修准备开业。听到这个消息后，我立即在大来戏院找到嘜根弟，并威胁他说，除非他还钱，否则我会向他的上级揭发他。那天他还了我200美元，并告诉我余款将按月分期偿还。因为我不想再与他发生纠纷，我同意了他的提议，然而在催收余款的过程中，我与他发生过几次争吵，因为他有时不肯付款。在这些场合， invariably (总是) 有刘富生 (Lau Foo Sung) 和刘阿明帮他争辩，刘富生在那里谋得了一份收票员的差事。截至目前，嘜根弟仍欠我55美元，我至今未能收回。

大约6个月前，刘富生搬到我隔壁居住，有一天他顺便提到他获得了给陈籟 (Mr. Chen Loh) 先生当保镖的职位。我承认在那次我取笑他为汉奸工作，但除此之外，我与这个人没有任何关系，也从未借给他一分钱。

关于他指控说1938年8月的某一天，他在虞洽卿路 (Yu Ya Ching Road) 的新世界外面遇到我，我要指出的是，在1938年7月底到10月初期间，我因严重的败血症卧床不起，在此期间

pages.en:
- 5 -
that time I was attended by Dr. Weng Sung Dau (王聲濤), M.D.,
who can be produced if necessary.
One very important point I omitted to mention in
my statement before is that just prior to the Chinese New Year
(February 19th, 1939) I had occasion to call at the Dah Lih
Theatre for the purpose of collecting the balance of the money
due to me, however on meeting Loh Kung Dee he refused to pay
me and I again threatened him with exposure. On this occasion
he told me to carry on and as a result I went home and typed
a letter to the Commissioner of Police, however after
reconsidering the matter I did not post it, however it has
been seized at my home this morning amongst the documents
seized, and I now identify the letter you show to me as such
(Exhibit I).
Regarding the raid on my house this morning, I
identify the Japanese interpreter who said to me, "If you don't
talk now, you will by and by" as a man, whom I saw in the
company of Lau Ngah Ming in the Sun Sun Hotel Ballroom about
two months ago.
Last but not least, in my own defence I would like
to point out that presuming I had been concerned in the crime
with which I am arrested, would it be feasible that I be so
stupid as to remain at my present address, when it was common
knowledge throughout the alleyway that Lau Foo Sang had been
arrested by the Japanese and Settlement Police on the 16/2/39.
I swear that this is my true statement and that the
accusations against me are absolutely false.
pages.zh:
- 5 -
由王声涛 (Weng Sung Dau) 医生诊治，如有需要他可以出面作证。
我在之前的陈述中遗漏了一个非常重要的点，就在中国新年前夕（1939年2月19日），我曾去大来戏院催收欠我的余款，然而见到嘜根弟时，他拒绝付款，我再次威胁要揭发他。那次他让我继续（指去告发），结果我回家后打了一封信给警务处处长，但经过重新考虑，我没有寄出，然而这封信今早在我家被搜查的文件中被查获，我现在确认你们给我看的这封信就是那一封（证物一）。
关于今早对我家的搜查，我认出那位对我说“如果你现在不说，以后也会说”的日本翻译，是大约两个月前我在孙孙饭店 (Sun Sun Hotel) 舞厅看到与刘阿明在一起的那个人。
最后但同样重要的是，为我自己辩护，我要指出，假设我卷入了我被捕所涉的罪行，我怎么会愚蠢到留在现在的住址，毕竟整条弄堂的人都知道刘富生 (Lau Foo Sang) 已于1939年2月16日被日本人和租界警察逮捕。
我发誓这是我的真实陈述，针对我的指控完全是虚假的。

pages.en:
C.D.S. 163, LOH SUNG DEE (李松棣) attached to
/self                                      Gordon Rd. Stn.
Gordon Rd. Stn.      25.3.39               transcribed Clerk Hsu.

I became acquainted with Koh Tsau Liang (郭老良) 15
years ago, as his mother was employed at that time as a
senior warderess of the S.J.D. Court Detention Cells.

Zau Ngoh Ming (赵鄂明) a native of Shanghai, who
before the hostilities was employed by a foreign company
on Szechuen Road as a comprador, intended to establish
a transportation company, but due to lack of fund, he, in
February 1938, asked me and Koh Tsau Liang to approach Koo
Wen Ching (顾文清) and one other named Tseeng (郑)
(both friends of Koh Tsau Liang) for a loan of $2000.00
payable within a period of 6 months, using a portion of his
inherited land in Yangtsepoo as security. The loan was
finally secured on the guarantee of Koh Tsau Liang and myself.
When the refund of loan was due, Zau Ngoh Ming failed to
return the whole amount of money to Koh Tsau Liang.

One evening in April 1938 Koh Tsau Liang had a row
with Zau Ngoh Ming over collection of debt, which resulted
in a fighting between these two men. Later I and Koh Tsau
Liang approached the two creditors, namely Koo and Tseeng
asked
and/them to allow us to refund the loan for Zau Ngoh Ming
which was agreed.

Following the closing down of the transportation Co.,
Zau Ngoh Ming became employed as an interpreter by certain
Japanese in Hongkew.

I came to know Zau Yee Hung 10 years ago, when he was
a fish merchant, trading between Yangchow and Shanghai.
He frequented the homes of my friends. Following the outbreak
pages.zh:
华捕头编号163，李松棣 (LOH SUNG DEE) 隶属
/本人                                      戈登路捕房
戈登路捕房      1939年3月25日               转录员：徐 (Hsu)

我认识郭老良 (Koh Tsau Liang) 已有15年，因为他的母亲当时受雇为上海司法拘留所 (S.J.D. Court Detention Cells) 的高级女看守。

赵鄂明 (Zau Ngoh Ming)，上海人，战前受雇于四川路一家外国公司担任买办，打算成立一家运输公司，但因缺乏资金，他于1938年2月请求我和郭老良去找顾文清 (Koo Wen Ching) 和另一位姓郑 (Tseeng) 的人（两人均为郭老良的朋友）借款2000美元，期限6个月，并以他在杨树浦的部分继承土地作为抵押。这笔贷款最终由郭老良和我担保得以落实。当还款到期时，赵鄂明未能向郭老良归还全部款项。

1938年4月的一个晚上，郭老良因催债与赵鄂明发生争吵，导致两人打架。后来我和郭老良找到两位债权人，即顾某和郑某，请求
允许我们替赵鄂明偿还贷款，他们同意了。

运输公司关闭后，赵鄂明受雇于虹口某些日本人担任翻译。

我认识赵义宏 (Zau Yee Hung) 已有10年，当时他是鱼商，在扬州和上海之间做生意。他常去我朋友家。随着当前

pages.en:
- 2 -
of current hostilities, Lau Foo Sung became unemployed.
He often requested me to introduce him to a job.
In March 1938 my younger brother, Loh Pau Hwa (陸寶華),
and several friends, entered partnership to establish the
"Dah Lih" (大利) Theatre. Through my introduction Lau Foo
Sung was employed there as ticket collector.
In June or July 1938 a friend of one named Kung (孔),
related to D.S.I. Tsu Peng Wei (朱彭威), attached to
Gordon Road Station, was desirous of employing two watch-
men, and I was asked by Mr. Tsu to enlist two honest men
for this position. Consequently I recommended Lau Foo Sung
and another man named Chu Yeong Ching (諸永清), who were
duly employed as day and night duty watchmen. After being
off duty Lau Foo Sung every day came to give assistance
to the staff of the Dah Lih Theatre.
As a result of booming business at the Dah Lih Theatre,
during the Chinese New Year Days, Lau Foo Sung was again
employed as ticket collector by management of this theatre.
Subsequently he was arrested.
Apart from the above I know nothing else.

Signed : LOH KUNG HEE
C.D.SolSS.
S.M.P.
pages.zh:
- 2 -
战事的爆发，刘富生 (Lau Foo Sung) 失业。
他经常请求我给他介绍工作。
1938年3月，我的弟弟陆宝华 (Loh Pau Hwa) 和几位朋友合伙成立了“大利” (Dah Lih) 戏院。经我介绍，刘富生受雇在那里担任收票员。
1938年6月或7月，一位姓孔 (Kung) 的朋友，与戈登路捕房的朱彭威 (Tsu Peng Wei) 警司有关系，希望雇佣两名更夫，朱先生请我招募两名诚实的人担任此职。因此我推荐了刘富生和另一位名叫诸永清 (Chu Yeong Ching) 的人，他们随即被聘为日班和夜班更夫。下班后，刘富生每天都来协助大利戏院的工作人员。
由于大利戏院生意兴隆，在春节期间，刘富生再次被戏院管理层聘为收票员。随后他被捕。
除上述情况外，我一无所知。

签名：罗公喜 (LOH KUNG HEE)
华捕头...
上海公共租界警务处

pages.en:
2nd Statement

ZAU P.OO SING (邵富生)
Zangchow                                D.S.I. Crighton
5 p.m.          23-3-39                 D.S.I. Soong Ping Tsung

At about 5 p.m. on the 21st March 1939 I was handed
over to the custody of the Japanese Military Police in Crime
Branch Headquarters and was taken to the 5th floor of Bridge
House where I was taken into an office occupied by three
Japanese. Immediately I entered this room one of the Japanese
asked me what I knew about the Chen Joh (陳鑠) assassination
and what I had done with the $7,000.00 reward money I had
received. I denied that I knew anything about this case, where-
upon the three Japanese set about me, one of them striking me
in the left eye with his clenched fist causing an abrasion to
same. I still denied that I knew of this case and eventually
they tied me down on a long form and for what I took to be half
an hour poured cold water down my nostrils. I still persisted
in my innocence whereupon they took the bonds from me and allowed
me to stand up. Later I was removed to the fourth floor, where
I was placed into a room resembling a cell. In this room were
eight other male Chinese whom I subsequently learned were being
detained as members of guerilla units. As I was very tired I
immediately went to sleep. The next day, i.e. 22-3-39, at about
1 p.m. I was again taken to the office on the 6th floor, where
one of the Japanese showed me a piece of paper bearing three
Chinese names :- Koh TsoLiang (郭志良), Tsang Loh Chuen
(章六見) and another named Dam Fung Wai (陶    ) and asked
me whether or not I had given information to these men which led
to the assassination of Chen Joh and whether or not they had
paid me the sum of $7,000.00. I denied this stating that I only
knew two men namely Koh Tso Liang and Tsang Loh Chuen, the latter
pages.zh:
第二份陈述

邵富生 (ZAU P.OO SING)
常州                                刑事调查处督察 Crighton
下午5时          1939年3月23日                 刑事调查处副督察 宋秉正

1939年3月21日下午5时许，我在刑事调查处总部被移交给日本宪兵队羁押，并被带至百老汇大厦（Bridge House）五楼，进入一间由三名日本人占据的办公室。我刚一进屋，其中一名日本人便问我关于陈籙（Chen Joh）遇刺案知道些什么，以及我如何处理收到的7,000.00美元赏金。我否认对此案有任何了解，于是这三名日本人对我动手，其中一人用紧握的拳头击打我的左眼，造成擦伤。我仍然否认知晓此案，最终他们把我绑在一张长凳上，在我认为约半小时的时间里，往我的鼻孔里灌冷水。我仍坚持自己是无辜的，于是他们解开绳索，让我站起来。随后我被带到四楼，关进一间类似牢房的房间。房间里还有另外八名中国男子，我后来得知他们因涉嫌属于游击队成员而被拘留。由于非常疲惫，我立刻睡着了。第二天，即1939年3月22日，下午1时许，我再次被带到六楼的办公室，一名日本人给我看一张写有三个中文名字的纸：郭志良（Koh TsoLiang）、章六见（Tsang Loh Chuen）和另一名名为陶    （Dam Fung Wai，原文名字残缺）的人，并问我是否向这些人提供了导致陈籙遇刺的情报，以及他们是否支付了我7,000.00美元。我予以否认，并称我只认识两个人，即郭志良和章六见，后者

pages.en:
- 3 -

I explained, was part owner of the Dah Lih (大来) Theatre,
Kweishow Road. They then questioned me as to what I knew about
these men, and in explaining my association with them I mentioned
that some time last year (1938) one named Lam Ngah Ming (趙鶴鳴)
through the introduction of C.D.S. Lok Hung Dee (陸根弟), had
borrowed $2,000.00 from Koh Tsoo Liang who in turn borrowed it
from Tsang Lok Chuen, supposedly for the purpose of opening a
cotton Brokerage, however this Hong had never been opened and
sometime later Koh Tsoo Liang and Lam Ngah Ming had had a fight,
when the latter stated he had given the money to a foreigner who
had misappropriated same. At this time Lam Ngah Ming went to
Louna Station and reported that he had been assaulted, but as to
what was the outcome of the whole thing I could not say. The
Japanese then wrote all this down on a statement form, which was
then passed to me for signature, and finger printing. This
having been completed, I was returned to the 4th floor but to a
different room, than the first one. On this occasion there were
two other prisoners beside me and I learned that they had been
arrested at San Ka Dee (曹家渡) for being in possession of
firearms.

On the third day, I was again taken to this office
on the 6th floor where I met three Japanese and one Chinese named
Man You Fung (毛友之), who explained that he was a member of the
S. M. Police. One of the Japanese then questioned me to the
effect that I had received $7,000.00 from the Chan Lok gang and
that I had given $4,000.00 of this to Lok Hung Dee, who in turn
had given me a job at $60.00 per month. I immediately denied
pages.zh:
- 3 -

我解释说，是贵州路大来（Dah Lih）戏院的合伙人之一。接着他们审问我关于这些人的情况，在解释我与他们的关系时，我提到去年（1938年）某个时候，一个叫赵鹤鸣（Lam Ngah Ming，音译）的人通过陆根弟（C.D.S. Lok Hung Dee）的介绍，向郭志良借了2,000.00美元，而郭志良又是从章洛泉（Tsang Lok Chuen，音译，注：前文为章六见，此处拼音略有不同，依原文保留）那里借来的，据称是为了开设一家棉花经纪行，然而这家商号从未开业，不久后郭志良和赵鹤鸣发生了争执，后者声称他把钱给了一个外国人，那人侵吞了这笔钱。当时赵鹤鸣去了老闸捕房报案称遭到殴打，但至于整件事的结果如何，我无法说明。日本人随后将所有这些内容记录在一份陈述表上，然后交给我签名并按手印。完成后，我被送回四楼，但不是第一个房间，而是另一个房间。这次除了我之外还有两名囚犯，我得知他们因持有枪支在曹家渡（San Ka Dee）被捕。

第三天，我再次被带到六楼的这间办公室，在那里我见到了三名日本人和一名名叫毛友之（Man You Fung）的中国人，他解释说自己是工部局警务处（S. M. Police）的成员。随后，一名日本人审问我，大意是我从陈乐帮（Chan Lok gang，音译）那里收到了7,000.00美元，并将其中4,000.00美元给了陆根弟，而陆根弟反过来给了我一份月薪60.00美元的工作。我立即否认

pages.en:
- 3 -

this, whereupon the Chinese answering to the name of Kan You
Vung told me not to be a fool, but to tell the truth that Tsang
Loh Chuen had shot Chen Lok and that if I did so he would
help me to get my freedom, whereas if I denied it I would be shot.
I then told her that I truly did not know of this case, where-
upon I was seized by the Japanese and tied down to a form and
had water poured down my nose again. After about 10 minutes
they released me and again questioned me as to whether or not
I knew Koh Tseu Liang. I at first denied I did but when they
produced a large knife and threatened to behead me I admitted
that I knew this man. During this time the man Kan You Vung
was present. I was again returned downstairs.

On the fourth day (26-3-38), I was again taken
upstairs at about 3 p.m., and on this occasion the Japanese
explained that I was being returned to the S.M.P. and that it
was necessary for me to be finger printed. He then finger
printed me, after which he gave me a bowl of rice, and some
vegetables. I was then returned to the cells. At about 6 p.m.
that night I was again removed from cells and taken to the office
where I was questioned by a Japanese regarding the particulars
of Koh Tseu Liang. I then gave them all the details concerning
that man, including his address. When this was completed the
Japanese again suggested that I had received money from Koh
Tseu Liang re the Chen Lok murder, but this I denied, but
explained that on one occasion when I met him near the Chinese
Company, he had jokingly accused me of being a traitor,
inasmuch that I was working for one. I was then returned to the
pages.zh:
- 3 -

了这一说法，于是那个名叫 Kan You Vung（音译，注：前文为毛友之 Man You Fung，此处拼音差异较大，依原文保留）的中国人告诉我不要犯傻，要说实话，说是章六见枪杀了陈乐（Chen Lok），如果我说出来，他会帮我获得自由，而如果否认，我就会被枪决。于是我告诉他我真的不知道这个案子，于是我被日本人抓住，绑在长凳上，再次往我鼻子里灌水。大约10分钟后，他们放开了我，再次审问我是否认识郭子良（Koh Tseu Liang）。起初我否认认识他，但当他们拿出一把大刀威胁要砍我的头时，我承认认识这个人。在此期间，那个叫 Kan You Vung 的人一直在场。我再次被带回楼下。

第四天（1938年3月26日，注：原文年份疑似笔误，应为1939年），下午3点左右，我再次被带上楼，这次日本人解释说我要被移交给工部局警务处（S.M.P.），并且需要按手印。于是他给我按了手印，之后给了我一碗饭和一些蔬菜。随后我被送回牢房。当晚6点左右，我再次被从牢房提出，带到办公室，一名日本人就郭子良的具体情况对我进行审问。于是我提供了关于那个人的所有细节，包括他的地址。完成后，日本人再次暗示我从郭子良那里收受了与陈乐谋杀案有关的钱款，但我予以否认，并解释说有一次我在中华公司附近遇到他时，他开玩笑地指责我是个叛徒，因为我正在为某人工作。随后我被送回

pages.en:
- 4 -

cells.

At about 4.30 p.m. 25-3-39, I was removed from
the cells and taken to upstairs where a Japanese threatened
me with a pistol if I did not talk. I told him I had nothing
further to say and that if he wanted to kill me he could do so.
He (Japanese) then commenced laughing and said that I was being
returned to the S. M. Police. I was returned to the S. M.
Police at 5 p.m. 25-3-39.

The aforegoing is my true statement.

Signed :- LAU FOO SENG.
pages.zh:
- 4 -

牢房。

1939年3月25日下午4点30分左右，我被从牢房提出并带到楼上，一名日本人用手枪威胁我，如果我不开口说话就开枪。我告诉他我没什么可说的了，如果他想杀我，可以动手。他（日本人）随即笑了起来，说我将被移交给工部局警务处（S. M. Police）。我于1939年3月25日下午5时被移交给工部局警务处。

以上是我的真实陈述。

签名：LAU FOO SENG（注：即邵富生）

pages.en:
TRANSLATION OF ATTACHED LETTER.

Dear Mr. Ts Liang,

At the time of the arrival of your note, I
was at the Zur Sung Temple. I returned to "Wu" only
last night. Regarding the "remarks" on the draft, I
have already visited the Commander-in-chief's Office
and requested Mr. Tsiang Tseh Ling to copy them all
down.

I learned that one Mr. Zung had recently been
appointed "special commissioner" of Canton. He has left
to take up the new post. Capt. Tsu might be appointed
by Provincial Government to fill the vacancy of a captain
for that authority. CAPt. Tsu is now on his way to "Wu".

Attached, please find a copy written by Tsiang
Teh Ming ................ ( not complete).
pages.zh:
附件信函译文。

尊敬的 Ts Liang 先生：

收到您的便函时，我正在祖松寺（Zur Sung Temple，音译）。我直到昨晚才回到“吴”（Wu，指苏州或吴县）。关于草案中的“备注”，我已经拜访了总司令办公室，并请蒋则灵（Tsiang Tseh Ling，音译）先生将它们全部抄录下来。

我获悉一位姓宗（Zung）的先生最近被任命为广州的“特派员”。他已离任赴新职。徐上尉（Capt. Tsu）可能会被省政府任命为该机构的空缺上尉职位。徐上尉目前正在前往“吴”的途中。

随信附上蒋德明（Tsiang Teh Ming）书写的一份副本 ____ （不完整）。

pages.en:
6th February, 1939.

Commissioner of C.I.D.,
S.M.P. Headquarter,
Foochow Road, Shanghai.

Dear Sir,

For your interest I wish to inform
you that there is a C.D.S. by the name of Mr. Lee
Kung Dee (陸根弟), in Gordon Road station. He
organized a secret resort, 864 Peking Road, 2nd
floor with his seconds, but there is a sign plate.
Nailed on the door such as Chi Chung Law Office
(濟眾法律事務所). However it is doing HUA WEI LOTTERY
(花會) affairs implicating with some offenders
and the detective obtaining $80 per month from the
above resort, if my word not really upon.

I hope you will detail a member of your
quarter to investigate the matter. I delete my
address name of on account of avoid some trouble.
pages.zh:
1939年2月6日。

致：
工部局警务处刑事调查处总监，
上海福州路工部局警务处总部。

尊敬的先生：

供您参考，特此告知，戈登路捕房有一名华籍侦探（C.D.S.）名为陆根弟（Lee Kung Dee，注：中文名确认为陆根弟，但拼音Lee对应李，此处依原文拼音及常见译名矛盾，按指令保留原文拼音对应的音译或已知中文名，此处已知为陆根弟，但拼音为Lee，可能存在档案错误，依指令“能确定的用当时通行的中文”，故译为陆根弟，但需注意拼音差异）。他与手下在北京路864号二楼组织了一个秘密场所，但门上钉着一块诸如“济众法律事务所”的招牌。然而，该处从事“花会”（HUA WEI LOTTERY）事务，牵涉一些罪犯，且侦探每月从上述场所获取80美元，所言非虚。

希望您派遣您属下的一名人员调查此事。为避免麻烦，我删去了我的地址和姓名。

re: at due to Japanese Military Police Headquarters.

J. I. Brighton J. I. Grubb.

In the afternoon of 24.3.39 Sgt. Major Hikiyi
of the Japanese Military Police Headquarters requested
assistance to visit a certain address on Amoy Road
at 6 p.m. on 24.3.39, for the purpose of arresting a
male Chinese, whose name at this time was not dis-
closed.

The usual formalities having been complied with
the undersigned was detailed to render the necessary
assistance.

At 6 p.m. 25.3.39, Sgt. Major Hikiyi accompan-
ied by three others called at Crime Branch Headquarters
and on being questioned regarding the source of his
information in relation to the arrest he wished to
make, he gave the following data.

At 4.30 p.m. on the 16.3.39 a male Chinese
named SAU POH LING (邵寶生) was arrested with the
assistance of French Headquarters on Kweichow
Road near Amoy Road (vide Misc. Report No. 52/39 C.1).
On the 21.3.39 this man was handed over to the Japanese
Military Police Headquarters, for a period of three
days and on the 24.3.39, application was made to the
S.M.Police for an extension of one day. During this
detention SAU POH LING would admit nothing during
the first three days. However, on the fourth day
although still denying having given the information
that subsequently led to the death of the late Mr.
Chen Lok (陳籙) Minister of Foreign Affairs, he
mentioned that in August 1938 outside the New World
pages.zh:
工部局警务处总部
C. I. WRIGHTON
第 57 号
日期 ____ 19__

工部局警务处特别分部 (D. C. Special Branch)
特别分部登记处 (S. B. REGISTRY)
编号 S.B. D.
日期 1939年3月25日。

事由：关于移交至日本宪兵队总部。

J. I. Brighton J. I. Grubb.

1939年3月24日下午，日本宪兵队总部的警部补（Sgt. Major）Hikiyi 请求协助，拟于1939年3月24日下午6时前往厦门路的某地址，目的是逮捕一名中国男子，其姓名当时未予披露。

在完成常规手续后，下列签署人被指派提供必要协助。

1939年3月25日下午6时，警部补 Hikiyi 在其他三人的陪同下前往刑事调查处总部，当被问及与他希望实施的逮捕有关的情报来源时，他提供了以下数据。

1939年3月16日下午4时30分，一名名为邵宝生（SAU POH LING）的中国男子在靠近厦门路的贵州路上，在法租界总部的协助下被捕（参见杂项报告第52/39 C.1号）。1939年3月21日，此人被移交给日本宪兵队总部，为期三天，1939年3月24日，向工部局警务处申请延长一天。在此期间，邵宝生在前三天拒不承认任何事项。然而，在第四天，虽然他仍然否认提供了随后导致前外交部长陈籙（Chen Lok）死亡的情报，但他提到，1938年8月，在新世界

pages.en:
- 2

on Yu Yeh Ching Road, he met a acquaintance named
**〔此处转录不清〕** an ex-police official of the
Nationalist Government, who, during the course of
the ensuing conversation, requested him to become
a member of a certain political party then operating
in Shanghai under his control. Continuing, Yau ( )
explained how he became a member of this certain
party, and how sometime later Oh Tseu Liang had
requested him to try and gain some information re-
garding the late Mr. Chen Loh and that should he
be successful in doing so, he would receive a monetary
reward of $2000.00. Yau further added that about this
time he borrowed $1000.00 from Oh Tseu Liang for
the purpose of establishing a transportation Company
and that over this he had quarrelled with Koh. After
some time this quarrel had been amicably settled
through the good offices of one named Tsang Loh Chuen
( ) who, it subsequently transpired, was another
prominent member of the same Political Party.

In concluding his statement Yau Yoh Sung (印：高华)
still denied that he had given the desired information
re the late Mr. Chen Loh, however, he did state that
should either of these two men be arrested the truth
in connection with this crime would be obtained.

Satisfied with the aforegoing explanation the
undersigned accompanied by D.S. Sugimoto, D.C. Yamahara,
D.S.I. Sung Ping Tsung (宋秉正), C.D.s Nos 189 and 274,
rendered the desired assistance to Sgt. Major Hikiyi
and party, and at 6.30 a.m. 28.3.39, proceeded to
pages.zh:
- 2

游乐场外的虞洽卿路（Yu Yeh Ching Road）上，他遇到了一位名叫 **〔此处转录不清〕** 的熟人，此人是国民政府的前警务官员，在随后的谈话中，此人要求他加入当时在上海由其控制的某个政党。接着，Yau（ ）解释了他如何成为该特定政党的成员，以及不久后欧子良（Oh Tseu Liang，注：前文为郭子良 Koh Tseu Liang，此处姓氏拼音不同，依原文保留）如何要求他设法获取有关已故陈籙先生的一些情报，并说如果他成功，将获得2,000.00美元的金钱奖励。Yau 还补充说，大约在这个时候，他向欧子良借了1,000.00美元用于成立一家运输公司，并因此与郭（Koh，注：原文此处又变回Koh）发生了争吵。一段时间后，这场争吵在一位名叫章六见（Tsang Loh Chuen）的人的斡旋下友好解决，后来证实此人也是同一政党的另一重要成员。

在结束陈述时，Yau Yoh Sung（印章：高华）仍然否认他提供了有关已故陈籙先生的所需情报，不过，他确实表示，如果这两人中的任何一人被捕，与该罪行有关的真相将会被查明。

对上述解释感到满意后，下列签署人在警探 Sugimoto、警探 Yamahara、刑事调查处副督察宋秉正（Sung Ping Tsung）、华籍侦探编号189和274的陪同下，向警部补 Hikiyi 及其随行人员提供了所需的协助，并于1939年3月28日上午6时30分，前往

ne 230 House 28, moy Road, where, in the down-
stairs back room one named **〔此处转录不清〕**
age 34, native of ootung, Unemployed, ex-police
official of the Nationalist Government, was taken
into custody. At the request of Sgt. Major Hsiyi
search of the room was made by S.P. Police and the
following seizures were:-

Twenty four letters in Chinese.
Eighteen papers in Chinese.
Fifteen visiting cards.
Four photographs.
One pair handcuffs.
one pistol holster.

The letters, documents etc are now being
perused, and those of any importance will be
listed and translated.

The arrested man when questioned by the
undersigned gave a verbal statement to the effect
that in 1905 he was born in Shanghai, and that
after studying in a Chinese Primary School located
in the French Concession, he subsequently entered
the Shanghai Municipal Council School for Chinese
at the age of 12 years and remained therein until
he attained the age of 16 years, after which he
entered the Shanghai Municipal Fire Brigade as
a Matron Clerk. After being employed in this
capacity for 2 years and on account of developing
sickness (Red eyes) he resigned, and some time later
pages.zh:
230号，莫利爱路（Moy Road）28号，在该处楼下后间，一名名为**〔此处转录不清〕**、34岁、广东籍、无业、前国民政府警务官员的男子被拘留。应警佐Hsiyi之请求，由特别巡捕（S.P. Police）对该房间进行了搜查，查获物品如下：

中文信件二十四封。
中文文件十八份。
名片十五张。
照片四张。
手铐一副。
枪套一个。

目前正查阅上述信件、文件等，其中重要者将列出并翻译。

被捕男子在接受本人讯问时作出口头陈述，大意如下：他于1905年出生于上海，在法租界的一所华童小学读书后，于12岁进入工部局华童公学，直至16岁。此后，他进入上海工部局消防队担任女舍监文员（Matron Clerk）。在此职位工作两年后，因患病（红眼病）辞职，不久之后

pages.en:
- 4 -

became employed as a telephone operator in the law
offices of Mr. Sandberg (?), 62 Jiangsu Road. A
few months later he resigned this position to become
employed as a clerk in the law offices of Mr. Lamiere
(?), French, at 34 Nanking Road, where he remained
for one year. In 1925, having obtained a position
of Chinese detective constable No. 85 with the Kuntse
City Police, under the Sun Chuen Sung (孙传芳)
Regime, he resigned from the last named job, and
from this time onward, until July 1937, when owing
to the outbreak of Sino-Japanese Hostilities he con-
tinued in the services of the Government as a police
officer at the following places:-
Chapei, Tashing Kampo, Nanking, Fushan, and
Suchow.
With the outbreak of hostilities he resigned his
position and returned to Shanghai where he has
remained unemployed, ever since.
Questioned regarding his source of income during
the past eighteen months this man stated that at time
of his father's death he had inherited some money, also
with his savings he had just managed to scrape through,
and that at the present moment he was financially em-
barrassed.
After having explained to this man the reason
for his arrest as outlined by Sgt. Major Hidayi, he
was questioned regarding his connections with Zen Foo
Sung (曾富生), and in reply, he stated that he first
pages.zh:
- 4 -

受雇于江苏路62号Sandberg先生（?）的律师事务所，担任电话接线员。数月后，他辞去该职，受雇于南京路34号法国人Lamiere先生（?）的律师事务所担任文员，为期一年。1925年，他在孙传芳政权下获得昆山县警察局第85号华探职位，随即辞去上一份工作。从那时起直到1937年7月，因中日战事爆发，他一直在以下地点的政府机构中担任警务人员：
闸北、大场营房、南京、福山和苏州。
随着战事爆发，他辞去职务返回上海，此后一直失业。
当被问及过去十八个月的收入来源时，此人称父亲去世时继承了一些钱款，加上积蓄勉强维持生计，目前经济拮据。
在向此人解释了警佐Hidayi所述的逮捕理由后，本人就其与曾富生（Zen Foo Sung）的关系进行了讯问，他回答说，他初次

pages.en:
met this man several years ago whilst the former
was employed as a tea-boy in the Chuh Wo (九華)
Lodging House, on Canton Road, then owned and
operated by ex- Det. Su Tung Fu (蘇東甫), now
at present undergoing a term of imprisonment for
larceny of woodoil (see Misc. Report No. 167/37 C.1),
and that recently he had had trouble with this man,
who, had about 6 months ago come to live next door
to him.

In making a complete denial of the allegations
against him, this man outlines in his written
statement the true facts of case, as is known to
him, and a perusal of same will show that the
foundation of these allegations appear to be a
quarrel over certain monies.

The complete statement will be forwarded with
next report.

Meanwhile the arrested man is being detained
at the request of the Japanese Military Police.

14.

D. S. I.
pages.zh:
见到此人是几年前，当时后者在广东路的九華（Chuh Wo）旅馆担任茶房，该旅馆由前探员蘇東甫（Su Tung Fu）拥有并经营，苏东甫目前因盗窃桐油罪正在服刑（参见杂项报告第167/37 C.1号），且最近他与此人发生过纠纷，此人约在6个月前搬至其隔壁居住。

在完全否认针对他的指控时，此人在其书面陈述中列出了他所知的案件真实情况，阅看该陈述可知，这些指控的基础似乎是一场关于某些钱款的争吵。

完整陈述将在下一份报告中附送。

与此同时，应日本宪兵队要求，被捕男子正被拘留。

14.

D. S. I.

March 28, 39.
FURTHER
ASSISTANCE TO JAPANESE MILITARY POLICE.

D. I. Konovaloff                                J. D. I. Grubb

As a result of the interview with Mr. Victor L.
Chen it was ascertained that no day's leave had been granted
to the suspect Lau Foo Sung (邵富生) and that as Mr. V. L.
Chen stated, Lau Foo Sung was definitely on duty at the
residence of the late Dr. Sion Loh (陳籙) on the date of
assassination from 9 a.m. to 12 noon, i.e. 19-2-39.

In view of this and the fact that the suspect Lau
Foo Sung still claimed that he was not on duty on the date of
assassination (19-2-39) an additional statement (attached) has
been taken from him. In this statement Lau Foo Sung has
accounted for his movements on the date of assassination.
According to his statement, the suspect had encountered during
the day of 19th February 1939 the following persons :-

(1). Loh Zang Keng    (陸長根), a teaboy employed at the
                      Tai Tseong (台衆) Dramatic Club,
                      854 Peking Road.

(2). Zung Ts Pah      (陳芝伯)
       &
(3). Tong Nyoh Pah    (唐玉發)
                      Both these persons are employed as
                      an accountant and a teaboy
                      respectively at the Dah Lai (大來)
                      Theatre, 863 Kweichow Road.

and (4). C.P.W. 2123, Au Sz Tseong (吳士忠), employed by
           a landlord of the premises
           situated in Lane 668, Yu Yuen Road.

All these four witnesses were located and carefully
questioned by the undersigned, C.D.S. 104 and J.D.S. Sugimoto
in presence of Sergt. Major Nikiri and his interpreter of the
Japanese Military Police Headquarters during the day of the 20th
March 1939.

The first witness, Loh Sang Keng, who, according to
the suspect Lau Foo Sung's statement, the latter met the witness
pages.zh:

D. C. (特别科).
H. Q. C. B.
1939年3月28日。
进一步
协助日本宪兵队。

D. I. Konovaloff                                J. D. I. Grubb

经与Victor L. Chen先生面谈，查明嫌疑人邵富生（Lau Foo Sung）并未获准休假一天，且正如V. L. Chen先生所述，在刺杀案发生当日，即1939年2月19日，上午9时至中午12时，邵富生确实在已故陈籙（Sion Loh）博士寓所执勤。

鉴于此，以及嫌疑人邵富生仍声称在刺杀案发生当日（1939年2月19日）未执勤这一事实，已从他那里获取了一份补充陈述（见附件）。在该陈述中，邵富生说明了他在刺杀案发生当日的行踪。根据其陈述，嫌疑人在1939年2月19日当天遇到了以下人员：

(1). 陸長根（Loh Zang Keng），北京路854号台衆（Tai Tseong）剧社雇佣的茶房。

(2). 陳芝伯（Zung Ts Pah）
       及
(3). 唐玉發（Tong Nyoh Pah）
                      这两人分别受雇于贵州路863号大來（Dah Lai）戏院，担任会计和茶房。

以及 (4). 华捕第2123号，吳士忠（Au Sz Tseong），受雇于虞园里（Yu Yuen Road）668弄内某房产的房东。

上述四名证人均已被找到，并于1939年3月20日当天，由本人、C.D.S. 104及J.D.S. Sugimoto在日本宪兵队本部Nikiri警佐及其翻译在场的情况下进行了仔细讯问。

第一名证人陆长根称，根据嫌疑人邵富生的陈述，后者于1939年2月19日上午9时在济众（Tsi Troong）剧社遇见了该证人

pages.en:
- 2 -

in the Tsi Troong Dramatic Club at 9 a.m. on the 19-2-39 and
paid him $1.00 as a Chinese New Year tip, stated that he had
seen Zau Foo Sung and received $1.00 from him on the day of
Chinese New Year i.e. 19-2-39 at a few minutes past 1 p.m. but
not in the forenoon. His statement is attached herewith.
The first and second named witnesses fully testified
that they both had seen and talked to Zau Foo Sung at the Dah
Lai Theatre, 263 Kweichow Road, between the hours of 10.45 a.m.
and 12 noon on the 19-2-39. Their statements appear to be
corroborating the suspect's and contradicting to Mr. V. L.
Chen's information where the latter avers that the suspect was
on duty between 8 a.m. and 12 noon on the 19-2-39.
The 4th witness C.P.W. 2123, stated that between the
hours of 7 a.m. and 7 p.m. on the 19-2-39 when he was on duty
in Lane 668, where the late Mr. Chen Loh's house is situated,
he did not see the suspect coming or leaving the lane, but had
seen Zau Foo Sung on the following day, i.e. 20-2-39 at 3 p.m.
and at 9 a.m. on the 23-2-39. Statement attached.
In his statement Zau Foo Sung avers that at 8.30 a.m.
on the 20-2-39 the following day after the assassination of Mr.
Chen Loh, he proceeded to the latter's residence, Lane 668, Yu
Yuen Road, and on entering the lane he encountered the C.P.W.
and during the ensuing conversation, he learned then about the
assassination of Mr. Chen Loh from this witness. This, however,
was denied by the C.P.W.
At the request of Sergt. Major Nikisi the suspect
Zau Foo Sung's wife named Zau Wong Sz (邵王氏), was summoned to
C.B.H.Q. (C.I.) offices and questioned regarding her husband's
pages.zh:
- 2 -

并付给他1.00元作为春节红包，但该证人陈述说，他是在春节当天，即1939年2月19日下午1点过几分见到邵富生（Zau Foo Sung）并收到其1.00元的，而非上午。其陈述附后。
第一和第二位具名证人充分作证，他们两人均于1939年2月19日上午10:45至中午12时之间，在贵州路263号大來戏院见到并与邵富生（Zau Foo Sung）交谈。他们的陈述似乎佐证了嫌疑人的说法，并与V. L. Chen先生的信息相矛盾，后者坚称嫌疑人在1939年2月19日上午8时至中午12时期间在执勤。
第四位证人，华捕第2123号陈述称，在1939年2月19日上午7时至下午7时他在陈籙先生故居所在的668弄执勤期间，并未看到嫌疑人进出该弄堂，但在次日，即1939年2月20日下午3时，以及1939年2月23日上午9时看到了邵富生（Zau Foo Sung）。陈述附后。
邵富生在其陈述中坚称，在陈籙先生遇刺后的第二天，即1939年2月20日上午8:30，他前往后者位于虞园里668弄的寓所，在进入弄堂时遇到了该华捕，并在随后的谈话中，从该证人口中得知了陈籙先生遇刺的消息。然而，这一点遭到了该华捕的否认。
应Nikisi警佐的要求，嫌疑人邵富生之妻邵王氏（Zau Wong Sz）被传唤至中央捕房总部（刑事调查科）办公室，并就其丈夫在

pages.en:
- 3 -

movements on the day of the assassination of Mr. Chen Luk,
i.e. 19-2-39. She fully corroborated the suspect's statement
with the exception that her husband was sick and confined to
bed during the day of the 18th February 1939. Her statement
is attached herewith.

An additional statement has been taken from the
2nd named suspect, Tang Hai Dah (鄧海大). In this statement
the suspect related as to how he became acquainted with the
1st named, Tau Poo Sung. This statement is attached hereto.

In accordance with instructions of D. C. (Crime)
the suspect Tau Poo Sung was handed over to the custody of
Sergt. Major Kateda of the Japanese Military Police Headquarters
at 5 p.m. on the 21st March 1939 for a period of 3 days (72
hours), against a receipt, which is attached hereto. In turn,
Sergt. Major Kateda was requested to procure a statement from
the chief bodyguard, Loo Da Ken Ts (盧大個子), who is at
present in the custody of Police Headquarters in Nanking.

In respect of the 3rd arrested, Yuh Shing Dah
(葉兴大), Sergt. Major Kateda stated that he can be now
released, whilst the 2nd arrested, Tang Hai Dah, still has to
be detained.

Enquiries proceeding.

H.G.

A. Konovaloff.
D. S. I.
pages.zh:
- 3 -

陈籙（Chen Luk）先生遇刺当日，即1939年2月19日的行踪接受讯问。她完全佐证了嫌疑人的陈述，唯一的例外是她丈夫在1939年2月18日当天生病卧床。其陈述附后。

已从第二名嫌疑人鄧海大（Tang Hai Dah）处获取了一份补充陈述。在该陈述中，嫌疑人讲述了他如何结识第一名嫌疑人陶庯生（Tau Poo Sung）。该陈述附后。

根据刑事科总监（D. C. (Crime)）的指示，嫌疑人陶庯生于1939年3月21日下午5时被移交给日本宪兵队本部Kateda警佐拘留，为期3天（72小时），并出具收据，收据附后。作为交换，已要求Kateda警佐从目前在南京警察总局拘留中的首席保镖盧大個子（Loo Da Ken Ts）处获取一份陈述。

关于第三名被捕者葉兴大（Yuh Shing Dah），Kateda警佐表示现可将其释放，而第二名被捕者鄧海大仍需拘留。

调查正在进行中。

H.G.

A. Konovaloff.
D. S. I.
